title: Add invocation fusion metrics and labeled-log tracer with adaptive alert dampening
author: Diego Marquez
description: Motivation: Long-tail noisy invocations and cross-tenant log flood make signal extraction for SLOs and cost attribution brittle. This change introduces two complementary observability primitives: 1) Invocation Fusion Metrics: runtime-side micro-aggregation that emits a compact per-invocation fingerprint and phased token emission histograms to attribute latency/cost across model stages without sampling every token. 2) Labeled-Log Tracer: a log enrichment path that attaches stable invocation labels (fingerprint, callsite-hash, model-variant-shadow id) to sampled log lines and spans to enable deterministic joins in dashboards. Goals: reduce cardinality explosion in dashboards, make alerting resilient to noisy tenants, and provide a low-cost way to reconstruct token-level latency/cost slices for investigation. What changed: - Serving runtime: add an optional InvocationFusion aggregator that computes a 128-bit fingerprint, per-phase token counts, and micro-latency sketches emitted as prometheus histograms and compact OTLP spans. The aggregator runs inline with request lifecycle but is gated by a config flag and budgeted CPU. - Tracing/logging: new labeled-log-tracer component that enriches existing span/log exporters with the fusion metadata and a tenant-stable short-id to allow cross-system joins. Added sampling filter to prioritize high-cost or anomalous invocations. - Telemetry pipeline: metrics mapping that turns fusion sketches into percentile rollups and a new downstream job that reconstructs token-latency deciles for dashboards without ingesting raw token traces. - Dashboards and alerts: a new dashboard (Invocation Fusion Explorer) with panels for per-phase token histograms, fusion fingerprint heatmap, tenant-noise quotient, and a cost-attribution panel. Alert dampening: introduce adaptive alert suppression rules that lower sensitivity for tenants with transient high-entropy fingerprints and escalate when consistent cost regressions are observed. - Tests and docs: unit and integration tests for the fusion aggregator, e2e smoke in the telemetry test harness, user-facing docs in observability guides, and a migration note for console users. Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated off by default; enable for internal staging traffic for 2 weeks. 2) Enable in canary for infra and platform tenants with metrics-only mode (no log enrichment) to evaluate overhead. 3) Gradually enable labeled-log-tracer for tenants that opt-in. Related work: builds on ENG-2098 (invocation summarizers) and SRE-121 alerting revamp. Notable constraints: we limit CPU budget per worker (default 0.5% of core) and cap emitted histogram cardinality to avoid increasing cardinality on prometheus. Observability cost: small increase in span metadata size but large downstream savings because token traces are sampled far less frequently. review_thread: Aisha Raman: Can we quantify CPU and latency tail impact for p99 under 1000rps during the canary? Diego Marquez: Added a microbench in tests/integration and a benchmark summary in the PR description; expected p99 +0.8ms on our c5g-like instances with default budget. Jonas Pritchard: Need to make sure prometheus cardinality is bounded if many tenants opt in; consider a hashed short-id bucketization. Diego Marquez: Implemented tenant-stable short-id with 256 buckets and added a config knob to limit histogram labels. Jonas Pritchard: Also add a circuit-breaker to disable fusion if CPU budget exceeded. Diego Marquez: Added circuit-breaker and simulated overload tests. Marta Li: Minor nits on telemetry mapping job logging; please add more metrics around failed sketch decodes. Diego Marquez: Added failure counters and retries. Marta Li: Approving after changes. CI: initial telemetry integration job failed on sketch flattener (parsing edge case), reran after fix and all checks passed. Merge: squash and merge after approvals, perform a staggered canary rollout following playbook.
release_notes: New: Invocation Fusion Metrics (compact per-invocation fingerprints and per-phase token histograms) and Labeled-Log Tracer for deterministic join keys in dashboards. Note: Feature is gated and opt-in; follow rollout runbook. Impact: small runtime CPU budget; reduces downstream trace ingestion needs and improves alert precision.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps fusion sketches compact and introduces config flags for tenants to opt-in to labeled logs. Operators should monitor fusion_cpu_overruns and sketch_decode_failures when enabling for new tenants.
